findings: Tabulated review of 26 previously published primary cutaneous myoepithelial carcinoma cases: ages ranged from 21 days to 85 years (median 58 years; mean 50.56 years, SD 24.70), with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 1:1.

Most patients were treated with primary excision; three received systemic therapy (one palliative chemotherapy, one resection plus adjuvant chemotherapy, one neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus resection); none received adjuvant radiotherapy.

Counted from the paper's Table 1 (the paper itself gives no totals): 8 of 26 cases are marked as having metastasis at presentation (5 of these as lymph node), 5 are marked as developing new metastases and 2 as local recurrence; follow-up, where reported, ranged from 3 to 132 months.
Reported sites include the back, the head, groin and lower extremities; tumor sizes in Table 1 ranged from 0.7 to 20 cm where reported.

A broad-spectrum keratin stain was positive in most cases tested, with two exceptions; calponin, S100 and p63 were variably positive or negative; desmin and melanocytic markers were negative in every case in which they were tested.
A BRAF V600E mutation was reported in one case; RNA fusion data were not available for any of the 26 reviewed cases.
Narrative discussion citing earlier reports, not a tabulated review of cases.
States that only 14 cutaneous myoepithelial carcinoma cases had been reported before this one (15 including it).
States that most reported cases involved female patients, suggesting a slight female predominance.
Reported age range 2.5 to 85 years, with a median age of 50 years.
States that cutaneous myoepithelial carcinoma appears to have a lower recurrence rate than its soft tissue counterpart (no figure given).
States that if complete resection is ultimately achieved before clinical metastasis, prognosis is good even after an inadequate first resection or a local recurrence.
Narrative discussion citing earlier reports, not a tabulated review of cases; states that fewer than 15 cutaneous cases had been reported.
Postsurgical local recurrence reported in up to 30% of cases and metastases in up to 15%; the authors note the true rates are difficult to estimate given the rarity of the tumor.
Most commonly reported on the head and neck and the lower extremities; slight female predominance; bimodal age distribution (before adulthood or after the fifth to sixth decades).
Reported tumor sizes range from 0.7 to 7 cm.
Surgical removal with clear margins is the treatment of choice, but no clear recommendation exists for margin width; PET scan and sentinel lymph node biopsy are considered advisable.

Chemotherapy and radiation results are described as variable and often ineffective; radiation monotherapy for recurrent or metastatic disease gave no significant benefit; Mohs surgery had not been described for myoepithelial carcinoma.
